2. Heard Sri Upendra Upadhyay, learned counsel for the applicant and Sri Ram Prakash Shukla,
learned counsel for the State and perused the material on record.
3. This is second bail application of the applicant.

The first bail application of the applicant was rejected by a co-ordinate Bench of this Court vide order dated 21.06.2022 passed in Criminal Misc.
Bail Application No. 20108 of 2022 (Raghuraj Alias Raghunath Singh and another vs. State of U.P.).

sentences.text: 4. This bail application under Section 439 of Code of Criminal Procedure has been filed by the applicant- Raghuraj Alias Raghunath Singh, seeking enlargement on bail during trial in connection with Case Crime No. 260 of 2021, under Sections 498-A, 304-B, 201 I.P.C. and Section 3/4 Dowry Prohibition Act, Police Station Pilua, District Etah.
5. Learned counsel for the applicant argued that the applicant is the father-in-law of the deceased Gulshan Devi.

It is argued that trial in the present matter has started in which 03 prosecution witnesses namely Smt. Mithilesh Kumar P.W.-1, Smt. Ratnesh P.W.-2 and Ranveer Singh P.W.-3 have been examined and all the said 03 witnesses have not supported the prosecution case and have been declared hostile, the copies of the statements of P.W.-1 & 2 have been placed before the Court which are annexed as Annexure-S.A.-1 to the supplementary affidavit dated 06.06.2023 and the copy of statement of P.W.-3 has been annexed as Annexure-S.A.-1 to the supplementary affidavit dated 08.01.2024.

Learned counsel has placed paragraph 13 of the affidavit in support of bail application and argued that the male members of the family including the applicant are in jail whereas co-accused who is the wife of the applicant is on bail vide order dated 21.06.2022 passed by this Court on the ground that an eight months old child was in jail with her.

It is further submitted while placing the same paragraph that the said child is now aged about 01 year & more than 02 months and it is very difficult for the wife of the applicant Smt. Rani Devi @ Rajrani to take care of herself and the child as she is poor and illiterate.
It is argued that the husband of the deceased namely Mohit Kumar @ Bhola is in jail.
The applicant has no criminal history as stated in para 18 of the affidavit and is in jail since 25.03.2022.
6. Per contra, learned counsel for the State opposed the prayer for bail.
7. After having heard learned counsel for the parties and perusing the record, it is evident that the present bail is the second bail application.
The first bail of the applicant was rejected by this Court vide order dated 21.06.2022 and by the same order the applicant no.2 therein namely Smt. Rani Devi @ Rajrani was granted bail.

The said order reads as under:-
"Heard Ms. Shashi Kumar Mishra, learned counsel for the applicants, Sri Sanjay Kumar Singh, learned AGA for the State and perused the material on record.

This bail application under Section 439 of Code of Criminal Procedure has been filed by the applicants Raghuraj alias Raghunath Singh and Smt. Rani Devi alias Rajrani,
seeking enlargement on bail during trial in connection with Crime No. 260 of 2021,
under Sections 498A, 304B, 201 I.P.C. and 3/4 D.P. Act, registered at P.S. Pilua,
District Etah.
Learned counsel for the applicants argued that the applicant no. 1 is father-in-law and the applicant no. 2 is mother-in-law of the deceased/Smt. Gulshan Devi.
It is argued that there are general and omnibus allegations against all the accused persons including the applicants.
It is further argued that the deceased died a natural death.
It is argued that the applicant no. 1 is an old man aged about 60 years, para-15 of the affidavit has been placed before the Court for the same.

Learned counsel has further Raghuraj Alias Raghunath Singh vs State Of U.P. on 12 February, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/97698174/
2 argued that the applicants were living separately and have no concern with the offences.

sentences.text: The deceased was living with Mohit Kumar@Bhola the son of the applicants in the village whereas the applicants were living separately in Delhi, para-16 of the affidavit has been placed before the Court for the same.

It is argued that from the wedlock of the deceased and Mohit Kumar @ Bhola, a girl was born who was aged about eight months and since there was no one in the house to take care of her, she is also in jail along with the applicant no. 2, in support of it para- 20 of the affidavit has been placed before the Court.
It is argued that Mohit Kumar @ Bhola is also in jail.
The applicant no. 2 is a lady and is entitled to the benefit of Section 437 Cr.P.C.
It is argued that the applicants have no other criminal antecedents as stated in para-22 of the affidavit and is in jail since 25.3.2022.
Per contra, learned State counsel opposed the prayer for bail and argued that the applicants are named in the F.I.R. and there are allegations against them.
It is argued that the deceased died in her matrimonial house after four years of marriage.
The dead body of the deceased was cremated and as such the same was not subjected to post mortem examination.
It is argued that the applicants are involved in the present matter.

In so far as the averments of para-20 of the affidavit are concerned which states that an infant of eight months being the daughter of the deceased is in jail with the applicant no. 2, the same is not disputed by learned State counsel.

After having heard learned counsels for the parties and perusing the record, it is evident that the applicants are named in the F.I.R. and there are allegations against them but looking to the facts and circumstances of the case particularly the averments made in para-20 of the affidavit that an eight months old child is in jail with the applicant no. 2, this Court is of the view that the applicant no. 2/Smt. Rani Devi alias Rajrani may be enlarged on bail.
Let the applicant no. 2/Smt. Rani Devi alias Rajrani, be released on bail in the aforesaid case crime number on her furnishing a personal bond and two sureties (one of the sureties to be a local person) each in the like amount to the satisfaction of the court concerned with the following conditions which are being imposed in the interest of justice:-
i) The applicant no. 2 will not tamper with prosecution evidence and will not harm or harass the victim/complainant in any manner whatsoever.
ii) The applicant no. 2 will abide the orders of court, will attend the court on every date and will not delay the disposal of trial in any manner whatsoever.
(iii) The applicant no.2 shall file an undertaking to the effect that she shall not seek any adjournment on the date fixed for evidence when the witnesses are present in court.
In case of default of this condition, it shall be open for the trial court to treat it as abuse of liberty of bail and pass orders in accordance with law.

sentences.text: (iv) The applicant no. 2 will not misuse the liberty of bail in any manner whatsoever.

In case, the applicant misuses the liberty of bail during trial and in order to secure her presence proclamation under section 82 Cr.P.C., may be issued and if applicant fails to appear before the court on the date fixed in such proclamation, then, the trial court shall initiate proceedings against her, in accordance with law, under section 174-A I.P.C.
(V)

The applicant no. 2 shall remain present, in person, before the trial court on dates fixed for (1) opening of the case, (2) framing of charge and (3) recording of statement under Section 313 Cr.P.C. If in the opinion of the trial court absence of the applicant is deliberate or without sufficient cause, then it shall be open for the trial court to treat such default as abuse of liberty of bail and proceed against her in accordance with law and the trial court may proceed against her under Section 229-A IPC.
(vi) The trial court may make all possible efforts/endeavour and try to conclude the trial expeditiously after the release of the applicant.

The identity, status and residential proof of sureties will be verified by court concerned and in case of breach of any of the conditions mentioned above, court concerned will be at liberty to cancel the bail and send the applicant no. 2 to prison.
Accordingly, the bail application with regard to the applicant is no. 2/Smt. Rani Devi alias Rajrani is allowed.

In so far as the applicant no. 1/Raghuraj Alias Raghunath Singh is concerned, looking to the facts and circumstances of the case, nature of evidence and gravity of offence, I do not find it a fit case to release him on bail.

Accordingly, the bail application of the applicant no. 1/Raghuraj Alias Raghunath Singh is rejected."
8.

The trial in the matter has started in which 03 prosecution witnesses including the first informant Smt. Mithilesh Kumar P.W.-1 has been examined who has not supported the prosecution case and has been declared hostile.
Mohit Kumar @ Bhola the husband of the deceased is in jail.

9. Looking to the facts and circumstances of this case, the nature of evidence and also the absence of any convincing material to indicate the possibility of tampering with the evidence, this Court is of the view that the applicant may be enlarged on bail.
10.
